| Podman and shell-entrypoint execution policy | Durable workspace and repository guidance classify `Caddy/tests/run.sh` as a Podman wrapper that must run outside the filesystem sandbox on its first attempt. Every tracked `Caddy/scripts/*.sh` and `Caddy/tests/*.sh` Bash entry point must be executable in both the working tree and Git index (`100755`); `executable-wrapper-policy-regression.sh` dynamically enumerates the full tracked set and rejects working-tree or index mode `0644` with positive and negative controls so local `core.fileMode=false` cannot hide CI failure |
| Pi-hole web URL roles | Required: `pihole-admin.local.theama.co` resolves to `10.1.0.56` and `fd36:5aa8:6971:1::56`, and those addresses are owned by the same `PIHOLE_IPV4`/`PIHOLE_IPV6` instances that own DNS VIPs `.55/::55`. The shared administration endpoint therefore always reaches the DNS owner without a separate backend certificate. `pihole0.local.theama.co` always exposes Node A's local Pi-hole UI and `pihole00.local.theama.co` always exposes Node B's local Pi-hole UI; each node-specific interface may be unavailable only when its corresponding host, Caddy, or Pi-hole application path is unavailable. Both Caddy services remain active, node-specific routes remain local, and raw lighttpd TCP 8080 remains loopback-only. Caddy health does not affect DNS election or ownership |

## Locked Decisions

- Deployment will proceed one authorized and validated action at a time.
- Both `CADDY_IPV4` and `CADDY_IPV6` instances on both nodes explicitly set
  `unicast_ttl 255`. Each reciprocal `unicast_peer` retains `min_ttl 255
  max_ttl 255`. The local directive controls advertisements when that node is
  the sender; the peer range validates advertisements when it is the receiver,
  so no configuration rewrite is required when MASTER and BACKUP roles change.
- Keepalived DBus enablement belongs only in the existing `global_defs` block
  of each authoritative main configuration. It must not be added to the Caddy
  fragment or create a second `global_defs`. Live installation is separately
  gated and requires read-only proof of compiled DBus support, an available
  system bus, exact main candidate bytes, and node-local rollback before any
  later one-node-at-a-time reload and DBus runtime acceptance.
- Keepalived's interval Caddy health helper checks only active Caddy service
  state and the bounded localhost HTTPS endpoint. Full `caddy validate` remains
  mandatory before configuration installation and Caddy reload, but is removed
  from the short VRRP polling path. Operator-supplied Node A instrumentation
  proves validation can exceed Keepalived's approximately four-second script
  boundary, receive `TERM`, return `143`, and repeatedly toggle failure/success.
  This deployment deviation prevents health-check overlap and VRRP flapping
  without weakening configuration admission validation.
- The Caddy `vrrp_script check_caddy` execution identity is explicitly
  `user keepalived_script caddy-tls`. Keepalived must not be expected to retain
  the account's supplementary `caddy-tls` membership when it executes the
  health check. Preflight and post-install validation must prove access to
  `/etc/default/caddy-ha`, the active full chain, and the active private key,
  followed by Caddy validation, localhost curl, and the complete helper under
  the exact health UID, primary `caddy-tls` GID, and cleared supplementary
  groups before any Keepalived reload can be authorized.
- Executable deployment definitions use the focused host tests and repository
  policies governing the changed boundary. Add the focused Debian 12 Podman
  slice only for Debian package/tool, identity, permission, mount, or runtime
  behavior. Documentation, journal, manifest-only metadata, accepted-hash, and
  workstation-consumer changes do not require it. The complete preserved
  historical host/Podman suite is not a deployment gate; current
  production-path validation plus applicable shared policies and current live
  evidence are authoritative. An unrelated historical replay failure is
  recorded but does not invalidate a passing current action unless it exposes a
  shared dependency or policy defect. Executed runners and retained evidence
  remain immutable, while reusable code and unexecuted local consumers may be
  corrected directly. Historical artifacts remain preserved for the
  post-deployment streamlining review.
- Workstation source ownership and container bind-projection ownership must be
  classified only through `tests/run-source-test-in-context.sh`: workstation
  execution requires `aaron:aaron:0755`; a validation-container read-only bind
  may appear as `root:root:0755` only with `CADDY_VALIDATION_CONTAINER=1` and
  the exact `/workspace/homelab-server-configs/Caddy` root. Immutable executed
  wrappers that predate this policy remain host-authoritative and must pass
  this centralized projection gate in containers; a bare skip marker is not a
  valid substitute.
- Every safety-critical decision gate in a live infrastructure transaction must
  emit a unique, stable label and its observed status before exit. This covers
  fallible command status, mutation, ownership, acceptance, rollback, recovery,
  and the final decision. Ordinary observations may be grouped into structured
  evidence. Repository regression tests must reject transactional drivers that
  cannot identify the exact failed decision without a follow-up live
  diagnostic; they need not turn every evidence field into a Boolean label.
- Caddy HA runtime state is boot-persistent through
  `/etc/tmpfiles.d/caddy-ha.conf`. `/run/caddy-ha` is `pi:caddy-sync:0750` so
  the inherited Keepalived notifier can write `vrrp-state` and `caddy-sync`
  can read but not alter it. `/run/caddy-ha-notify` is `pi:pi:0700` for the
  notifier's duplicate-suppression state. Type `d`, not `D`, is mandatory so
  boot creation and ownership repair cannot truncate retained runtime content.
- Every live command stream that affects transactional acceptance must be
  captured and classified during that same run. Before any emptiness or content
  gate, the transaction or runner must emit independently labeled bounded byte
  count, line count, SHA-256, and safe classification records for stdout and
  stderr. Metadata alone is not a secured evidence outcome. After
  classification, bounded, printable, secret-free, path-safe content must be
  emitted between explicit begin/end labels or retained at a reported
  protected path with exact owner, mode, and hash. Unsafe content remains
  suppressed and may be retained only for separately authorized protected
  inspection. Empty streams are recorded explicitly. Rollback and cleanup must
  not delete the only useful capture before one of these outcomes is secured.
  The historical Action 17s deficiency is retained only behind exact
  transaction SHA-256
  `325a8fff552646073768a619f5ee793423494d7258c8503624f1b44be0a0e5d8`;
  the metadata-only Action 17s retry is retained behind exact transaction
  SHA-256
  `269c48158969f3767b13ffa92aaef1559bcb0c25c64bb19fdb93e70f56713bd0`.
  Changed or new transactions must pass the transaction-output evidence policy.
  A corrected finalizer must keep its forced-command stdout silent by
  suppressing successful `caddy validate` stdout, while its caller still
  records both complete finalizer streams during the original transaction.
- Synchronization transport bootstrap names must not depend solely on the DNS
  service they help maintain. Node B maps only Node A's physical IPv4 and
  stable ULA to `pihole0.local.theama.co` in a bounded managed `/etc/hosts`
  block. A later separately defined and authorized Node A action will map only
  Node B's physical addresses to `pihole00.local.theama.co`. VIPs are excluded.
  These mappings supplement authoritative DNS for restricted SSH, rsync, and
  lsyncd bootstrap; they do not replace DNS.
- Action 17m must not read, rewrite, or infer ownership of `/etc/resolv.conf`.
  Resolver-manager provenance is not yet established on both nodes. Stable ULA
  AAAA/PTR authority and physical-peer `/etc/hosts` bootstrap are sufficient
  for this bounded correction.
- The DNS hosts must use their local Pi-hole as their primary operating-system
  resolver and the peer's physical IPv4 address as fallback: Node A uses
  `127.0.0.1` then `10.1.0.54`; Node B uses `127.0.0.1` then `10.1.0.53`.
  Each Pi-hole continues to use its node-local Unbound instance at
  `127.0.0.1#5335`. Ordinary LAN clients use the Pi-hole DNS VIP. The DNS
  hosts must not normally use the DNS VIP or public resolvers; public DNS is
  temporary break-glass only because it cannot answer `local.theama.co` and
  would leak internal queries. Before implementing this topology, a separate
  read-only gate must identify the active Debian resolver manager, confirm the
  local Pi-hole listener, establish service boot ordering, and determine the
  supported persistent configuration path. Do not directly edit
  `/etc/resolv.conf` or represent this requirement as deployed before that
  inspection and a separately authorized transaction succeed.
- Nodes A and B run Pi-hole v5, not Pi-hole v6. Do not use v6-only
  `pihole.toml` or `pihole-FTL --config` interfaces in this deployment.
  Following any Unbound local-zone activation or reload, reset the node-local
  Pi-hole resolver/cache before evaluating Pi-hole-path DNS acceptance, because
  cached positive or negative answers can otherwise invalidate the gate.
  The reset must use the supported Pi-hole v5 interface discovered on the
  target node, is a service/cache mutation, and therefore belongs inside a
  separately authorized transaction with readiness and rollback evidence.
  Read-only diagnostics may prove that `pihole restartdns` is installed but
  must not invoke it.
- Workstation validation images must declare every command exercised by
  in-container repository runners and assert each command at integration
  startup. Git is installed in `Caddy/tests/Containerfile`, and the exact
  Git-based ignored/untracked source proof runs on both host and Podman. Do not
  add workstation validation-only packages to the hash-pinned live-node
  dependency manifest.
- Dynamically generated assertion labels must be normalized to the exact
  grammar accepted by their workstation validator, and regression fixtures
  must include every production token class, including command names with
  hyphens. A generic underscore-only fixture is insufficient.
- A recognized, regression-pinned workstation wrapper false positive that
  cannot affect remote evidence, secret safety, or cleanup is an advisory and
  does not fail an otherwise authoritative gate. Remote nonzero status,
  missing, duplicate, malformed, unsafe, or mismatched remote evidence,
  cleanup failure, and any unknown workstation validation defect remain
  fail-closed. An advisory never substitutes for independent remote readback.
- Podman and repository validation wrappers that invoke Podman require the
  rootless runtime below `/run/user` and must be launched with first-attempt
  filesystem-sandbox escalation. Do not perform a known-to-fail sandbox probe
  before the permitted invocation. Keep escalation scoped to the exact Podman
  command or repository validation wrapper.
- A function-local shell variable must never reuse a script-level readonly
  variable name, regardless of declaration order. Host and Podman validation
  must run the repository collision-policy test. Historical immutable
  collisions may remain only in an exact path/name/SHA-256 allowlist; any
  content change, new variable, or new file collision fails validation.
- Shell formatting writes must use
  `Caddy/tests/shfmt-canonical.sh --write FILE [FILE ...]`; bare `shfmt -w` is
  prohibited. The wrapper pins `-i 4 -ci`, requires explicit regular files,
  rejects symlinks and paths outside the server repository plus its explicit
  Munin dependency, and is shared by pre-commit and the Caddy host suite.
- Live Munin monitoring is a post-deployment phase. Do not install, configure,
  enable, or validate Caddy/lsyncd Munin plugins on either node or the Munin
  master until core Caddy deployment acceptance has been declared through a
  separate authorization gate. Repository-only lint and fixture validation may
  continue and are not evidence of live monitoring deployment.
- Home Assistant Yellow remains on automatic IPv6 during the core Caddy
  deployment. Do not publish its ISP-derived global or link-local IPv6
  addresses. After core Caddy deployment acceptance and under separate
  authorization, define the dual-stack allocation convention, perform
  duplicate-address and reachability checks, add a permanent ULA while
  retaining SLAAC and Router Advertisement behavior, validate reboot
  persistence, and only then add its AAAA and IPv6 PTR records. This
  post-deployment work must not use the HAOS `Static` selection if doing so
  replaces automatic Router Advertisement and SLAAC processing.
- Node A two-file Unbound adoption must use candidate primary hash
  `cef0349528f87e97362c5917f1d0f77baca92eebf04790ed96997dfe3a0dd2e8`
  and local-zone hash
  `8a7d1c6d2235e6f37a98dfd3e10165b49968fcc5f3e898ce0b359f70bc0456d1`.
  The approved candidate values are `dnstap-enable: no`,
  `edns-buffer-size: 1232`, `harden-algo-downgrade: no`,
  `harden-large-queries: no`, and absolute terminal-root-dot targets for all
  active `local-data-ptr` records.
- Node A adoption follows the validated Node B separation: Action 17i stages
  only the primary fragment at
  `/var/tmp/caddy-unbound-node-a-action17i-primary`. The local-zone fragment
  is reserved for later Action 17j at
  `/var/tmp/caddy-unbound-node-a-action17j-local-zone`; Action 17i must prove
  that path remains absent.
- Action 17i must start its privileged remote shell at `/`, emit one unique
  label for each of 76 fail-closed assertions, pass the readonly/local
  collision policy, use normalized state hashing, stop immediately if its
  transaction directory is not safely created, retain no remote source stage,
  and classify incomplete rollback evidence as exit `125`.
- Node A Action 17j must depend on the exact accepted Action 17i stage,
  including its directory/file modes, primary candidate hash, manifest,
  metadata hashes, and completion marker. It stages only
  `pihole-local-zone.conf` at
  `/var/tmp/caddy-unbound-node-a-action17j-local-zone`.
- Action 17j must validate exactly 64 uniquely labeled preflight assertions
  and 90 total assertions, the approved 23 `local-data` records, 20
  `local-data-ptr` records with absolute terminal-dot targets, and the
  protected combined two-file parser before mutation. It must use normalized
  state hashing, `cd /`, no-clobber promotion, Action-owned rollback, remote
  source cleanup, collision-policy checks, and exit `125` for incomplete
  rollback. It must neither transfer the primary source again nor activate,
  reload, query, or mutate any live DNS service.
- Independent Action 17j-a must stream its inspector directly from `/`, create
  no remote path, verify exactly 70 unique assertions, validate the exact
  Action 17i and 17j file sets/content/metadata/manifests, parse the combined
  candidates through `/dev/stdin`, and collect the accepted live state twice
  using normalized hashing. Its workstation classifier must preserve complete
  semantic mismatch evidence as status `1`; only malformed, incomplete,
  duplicated, unsafe, or status-inconsistent evidence is classified as `97`.
- The living plan remains at `Caddy/docs/caddy_plan-v1.1.md`.
- After local hash, source, and contract gates pass, an explicitly authorized
  command whose defined purpose requires SSH or API access to the home-lab LAN
  must be launched with network escalation on its first attempt. The escalation
  grants only workstation network access; it does not broaden the authorized
  command, target, privileges, mutation scope, or retry authority. If that
  permission is unavailable, stop before execution rather than generating a
  known sandbox-only transport failure.
- Repository tooling is idempotent and supports dry-run, rollback, and uninstall.
- TLS secrets are sourced from Doppler project `homelab-dev`, config `prd_caddy`.
- Doppler is installed and used only on the Ubuntu operator workstation; neither
  Caddy node receives the Doppler package or credentials.
- Caddy serves HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3; firewall intent includes UDP 443.
- Runtime services and scripts log only through systemd-journald.
- Node-specific Pi-hole names remain available in addition to the shared HA name.
- Unbound configuration is a two-file prerequisite with explicit ownership:
  `/etc/unbound/unbound.conf.d/pihole.conf`, sourced from workstation
  `Unbound/configs/pihole0.conf`, owns resolver, listener, forwarding, cache,
  hardening, and observability behavior; and
  `/etc/unbound/unbound.conf.d/pihole-local-zone.conf`, sourced from
  workstation `Unbound/configs/pihole0-local-zone.conf`, owns
  `local.theama.co` policy and A, AAAA, PTR, and SRV data. Each top-level
  fragment retains its own `server:` clause.
- The retained Action 17f artifact remains
  `/var/tmp/caddy-unbound-node-b-action17f-local-zone/pihole0-local-zone.conf`
  for historical hash continuity. Action 17g installs those exact bytes under
  the corrected live name `pihole-local-zone.conf`. The nonexistent filename
  `pihole00-local-zone.conf` is outside the action and is not checked.
- Both live nodes currently use a single Unbound configuration file, as
  confirmed by the user. The two workstation files describe the intended
  split state and must not be represented as deployed until Node B and then
  Node A are separately migrated and validated.
- Adopt and validate the two-file Unbound prerequisite on Node B and then
  Node A through separately authorized actions before any Caddy DNS record
  deployment or synchronization retry. This plan entry does not authorize a
  file installation, DNS record addition, Unbound validation/reload, Pi-hole
  change, or service mutation.
- `pihole-admin.local.theama.co` uses the Caddy VRRP VIPs `10.1.0.56` and
  `fd36:5aa8:6971:1::56`; Caddy proxies to the active node's loopback Pi-hole
  web backend. The existing `.55/::55` Pi-hole VIP remains the DNS VIP.
- UniFi read-only collection uses local API key name `audit` with Doppler
  reference `homelab-dev/prd_unifi:AUDIT`; the key value is never recorded.
- Caddy client access is limited to Default LAN VLAN 1; IoT VLAN 200 and Guest
  VLAN 400 are excluded.
- lighttpd is installed and managed as a Pi-hole artifact. Caddy deployment
  must not replace or independently manage the package, must preserve the
  current Pi-hole PHP/FastCGI tree, and must revalidate/regenerate its derived
  loopback candidate after Pi-hole upgrades.
- Material security, network, interface, behavior, scope, or ownership deviations
  require approval; minor mechanical deviations are recorded with rationale.

### Runtime-directory correction Actions 20e and 20e-a

The original Action 20e was executed once and stopped before mutation because
Debian 12 `systemd-tmpfiles` does not support `--dry-run`. Its exact outer
SHA-256 `466cf7b94eb930bb87e6ad14c35a3654cef9f1302a343cb83cebf758212b0b7f`

Local source comparison proved the root cause. The immutable Action 17f driver
uses:

```bash
state_hash=$(live_state | sha256sum | awk '{ print $1 }')
```

That hashes the final newline emitted by `live_state`. The accepted inspector
uses command substitution to capture `live_state`; Bash removes trailing
newlines, and the inspector then hashes the normalized bytes with
`printf '%s'`. The two hashes are therefore deterministically different even
though the collected system state is identical.

remained at the accepted Action 17e persistent state. At that point, the next
gate required separate authorization to define—but not execute—an append-only
corrected bounded Action 17f retry using the accepted normalized hashing
semantics. That definition was later authorized and is recorded below;
execution remains unauthorized.

  sha256sum --check --status
printf '%s  %s\n' "$expected_source_sha" "$staged_source" |
  sha256sum --check --status

primary_fingerprint() {
  gpg --homedir "$gpg_home" --batch --with-colons --show-keys "$1" |
    awk -F: '
      $1 == "pub" { want_fingerprint = 1; next }
      want_fingerprint && $1 == "fpr" && !printed {
        print $10
        printed = 1
        want_fingerprint = 0
      }
    '
}

[[ "$(grep -Fxc "$expected_deb" "$staged_source")" -eq 1 ]]
[[ "$(grep -Fxc "$expected_deb_src" "$staged_source")" -eq 1 ]]

gpg --homedir "$gpg_home" --batch --yes --dearmor \
  --output "$staged_keyring" "$raw_key"
printf '%s  %s\n' "$expected_keyring_sha" "$staged_keyring" |
  sha256sum --check --status
[[ "$(primary_fingerprint "$staged_keyring")" == "$expected_fingerprint" ]]

install -o root -g root -m 0644 -- "$staged_keyring" "$key_target"
key_created=true
install -o root -g root -m 0644 -- "$staged_source" "$source_target"
source_created=true

[[ "$(stat -c '%U:%G:%a' -- "$key_target")" == root:root:644 ]]
[[ "$(stat -c '%U:%G:%a' -- "$source_target")" == root:root:644 ]]
printf '%s  %s\n' "$expected_keyring_sha" "$key_target" |
  sha256sum --check --status
printf '%s  %s\n' "$expected_source_sha" "$source_target" |
  sha256sum --check --status
[[ "$(primary_fingerprint "$key_target")" == "$expected_fingerprint" ]]
[[ "$(grep -Fxc "$expected_deb" "$source_target")" -eq 1 ]]
[[ "$(grep -Fxc "$expected_deb_src" "$source_target")" -eq 1 ]]

success=true
rm -rf -- "$work_dir"
trap - EXIT
[[ ! -e "$work_dir" ]]

sha256sum -- "$key_target" "$source_target"
printf 'caddy_repository_files_installed=true\n'
NODE_A_CADDY_REPOSITORY_INSTALL

    awk -F '\t' '$1 != "caddy"' |
    sort
}

protected_service_state() {
  for service in \
    lighttpd.service keepalived.service ssh.service unbound.service \
    pihole-FTL.service munin-node.service; do
    printf '### %s\n' "$service"
    systemctl show "$service" --no-pager \
      -p ActiveState -p SubState -p MainPID -p NRestarts
  done
}

rollback() {
  original_rc=$?
  trap - EXIT
  if [[ "$transaction_complete" == true ]]; then
    return
  fi

  set +e
  printf 'caddy_install_rollback_started=true\n' >&2
  rollback_failed=false

  systemctl stop caddy.service caddy-api.service >/dev/null 2>&1
  current_status=$(package_status)
  if [[ -n "$current_status" && "$current_status" != 'un ' ]]; then
    DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive NEEDRESTART_MODE=l \
      apt-get purge --yes caddy
    purge_rc=$?
    if ((purge_rc != 0)); then
      rollback_failed=true
    fi
  fi

  if [[ "$policy_created" == true ]]; then
    rm -f -- "$policy_target"
    policy_created=false
  fi
  current_status=$(package_status)
  if [[ -z "$current_status" || "$current_status" == 'un ' ]]; then
    if [[ "$package_install_started" == true ]]; then
      rm -rf -- /etc/caddy /var/lib/caddy /var/log/caddy
    fi
    if [[ "$masks_created" == true ]]; then
      systemctl unmask caddy.service caddy-api.service >/dev/null 2>&1
    fi
    systemctl daemon-reload
    for target in \
      /usr/bin/caddy \
      /lib/systemd/system/caddy.service \
      /lib/systemd/system/caddy-api.service \
      /etc/systemd/system/caddy.service \
      /etc/systemd/system/caddy-api.service; do
      if [[ -e "$target" || -L "$target" ]]; then
        rollback_failed=true
      fi
    done
  else
    systemctl mask caddy.service caddy-api.service >/dev/null 2>&1
    systemctl daemon-reload
    rollback_failed=true
  fi

  if [[ -n "$work_dir" && -d "$work_dir" ]]; then
    rm -rf -- "$work_dir"
  fi

  if [[ -z "$current_status" || "$current_status" == 'un ' ]]; then
    if getent passwd caddy >/dev/null ||
      getent group caddy >/dev/null; then
      rollback_failed=true
    fi
    for target in \
      /usr/bin/caddy \
      /etc/caddy \
      /var/lib/caddy \
      /var/log/caddy \
      /lib/systemd/system/caddy.service \
      /lib/systemd/system/caddy-api.service \
      "$policy_target"; do
      if [[ -e "$target" || -L "$target" ]]; then
        rollback_failed=true
      fi
    done
    [[ "$(protected_service_state)" == "$services_before" ]] ||
      rollback_failed=true
    [[ "$(ss -H -lntup | sort)" == "$listeners_before" ]] ||
      rollback_failed=true
    current_protected_hashes=$(
      sha256sum -- \
        /etc/lighttpd/lighttpd.conf \
        /etc/lighttpd/conf-enabled/external.conf \
        /etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf
    )
    [[ "$current_protected_hashes" == "$protected_hashes_before" ]] ||
      rollback_failed=true
  fi

  if [[ "$rollback_failed" == true ]]; then
    systemctl mask caddy.service caddy-api.service >/dev/null 2>&1
    systemctl daemon-reload
    printf 'caddy_install_rollback_complete=false\n' >&2
    printf 'Caddy masks were retained for listener safety.\n' >&2
    exit 97
  fi
  printf 'caddy_install_rollback_complete=true\n' >&2
  exit "$original_rc"
}

[[ -f "$key_target" && ! -L "$key_target" ]]
printf '%s  %s\n' "$expected_source_sha" "$source_target" |
  sha256sum --check --status
printf '%s  %s\n' "$expected_keyring_sha" "$key_target" |
  sha256sum --check --status
policy=$(apt-cache policy caddy)
candidate=$(
  awk '/^[[:space:]]*Candidate:/ { print $2; exit }' <<<"$policy"
)
[[ "$candidate" == "$expected_version" ]]
grep -Fq 'https://dl.cloudsmith.io/public/caddy/stable/deb/debian' \
  <<<"$policy"
grep -Fxq 'Architecture: arm64' \
  < <(apt-cache show "caddy=$expected_version")

package_status=$(
  dpkg-query -W -f='${db:Status-Abbrev}' caddy 2>/dev/null || true
)
printf 'caddy_dpkg_status=%q\n' "$package_status"
[[ -z "$package_status" || "$package_status" == 'un ' ]]
dpkg_audit=$(dpkg --audit)
[[ -z "$dpkg_audit" ]]
if apt-mark showmanual | grep -Fxq caddy; then
  printf 'Caddy remains manually marked.\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

mapfile -t dpkg_info_residue < <(
  find /var/lib/dpkg/info -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 \
    \( -type f -o -type l \) -name 'caddy.*' -print |
    sort
)
if ((${#dpkg_info_residue[@]} != 0)); then
  printf 'Unexpected dpkg Caddy residue: %s\n' \
    "${dpkg_info_residue[@]}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if getent passwd caddy >/dev/null ||
  getent group caddy >/dev/null; then
  printf 'Unexpected active identity: caddy\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi
if getent group www-data |
  awk -F: '{ print $4 }' |
  tr ',' '\n' |
  grep -Fxq caddy; then
  printf 'Caddy remains in the www-data group.\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

active_identity_files=(
  /etc/passwd /etc/group /etc/shadow /etc/gshadow /etc/subuid /etc/subgid
)
for file in "${active_identity_files[@]}"; do
  if [[ -f "$file" ]] && identity_file_contains_caddy "$file"; then
    printf 'Active identity file contains Caddy: %s\n' "$file" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

backup_identity_files=(
  /etc/passwd- /etc/group- /etc/shadow- /etc/gshadow-
  /etc/subuid- /etc/subgid-
)
identity_backup_residue_count=0
for file in "${backup_identity_files[@]}"; do
  residue=false
  if [[ -f "$file" ]] && identity_file_contains_caddy "$file"; then
    residue=true
    ((identity_backup_residue_count += 1))
  fi
  printf 'identity_backup_contains_caddy=%s:%s\n' "$file" "$residue"
done

for target in \
  /usr/bin/caddy \
  /etc/caddy \
  /var/lib/caddy \
  /var/log/caddy \
  /var/mail/caddy \
  /usr/share/caddy \
  /usr/share/doc/caddy \
  /usr/share/man/man8/caddy.8.gz \
  /usr/share/bash-completion/completions/caddy \
  /usr/share/fish/vendor_completions.d/caddy.fish \
  /usr/share/zsh/vendor-completions/_caddy \
  /lib/systemd/system/caddy.service \
  /lib/systemd/system/caddy-api.service \
  /etc/systemd/system/caddy.service \
  /etc/systemd/system/caddy-api.service \
  /usr/sbin/policy-rc.d; do
  if [[ -e "$target" || -L "$target" ]]; then
    printf 'Unexpected Caddy rollback target: %s\n' "$target" >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

mapfile -t systemd_residue < <(
  find /etc/systemd /var/lib/systemd -xdev \
    \( -type f -o -type l \) -iname '*caddy*' -print |
    sort
)
if ((${#systemd_residue[@]} != 0)); then
  printf 'Unexpected systemd Caddy residue: %s\n' \
    "${systemd_residue[@]}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

unit_state=$(
  for unit in caddy.service caddy-api.service; do
    printf '%s:%s:%s:%s\n' \
      "$unit" \
      "$(systemctl show --property=LoadState --value "$unit")" \
      "$(systemctl is-active "$unit" 2>/dev/null || true)" \
      "$(systemctl is-enabled "$unit" 2>/dev/null || true)"
  done
)
printf '%s\n' '--- Caddy unit state ---'
printf '%s\n' "$unit_state"
grep -Eq '^caddy[.]service:not-found:inactive:(|not-found)$' <<<"$unit_state"
grep -Eq '^caddy-api[.]service:not-found:inactive:(|not-found)$' \
  <<<"$unit_state"
if pgrep -x caddy >/dev/null; then
  printf 'Unexpected Caddy process.\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi

printf '%s  %s\n' \
  568507d5604cb2794106de3de29d1603c3f12c9045bf7fc1ad4342592a1395c1 \
  /etc/lighttpd/lighttpd.conf |
  sha256sum --check --status
printf '%s  %s\n' \
  6da587363054a4db69fb742d23bddde06aec866e11fb7a91bff1a8d75a713f7a \
  /etc/lighttpd/conf-enabled/external.conf |
  sha256sum --check --status
printf '%s  %s\n' \
  cf4858888ae80772f1a50dda7c0ea120ff083eafae33a0ad4ca291d44755c1e2 \
  /etc/keepalived/keepalived.conf |
  sha256sum --check --status

for service in lighttpd keepalived ssh unbound pihole-FTL munin-node; do
  systemctl is-active --quiet "$service"
  printf 'protected_service_active=%s\n' "$service"
done

lighttpd_pid=$(systemctl show --property=MainPID --value lighttpd.service)
[[ "$lighttpd_pid" =~ ^[1-9][0-9]*$ ]]
tcp_frontend=$(
  ss -H -ltnp |
    awk '$4 ~ /:80$|:443$/ { print }' |
    sort
)
printf '%s\n' '--- TCP 80/443 listeners ---'
printf '%s\n' "$tcp_frontend"
[[ -n "$tcp_frontend" ]]
if grep -Fv 'users:(("lighttpd"' <<<"$tcp_frontend"; then
  printf 'A non-lighttpd process owns TCP 80 or 443.\n' >&2
  exit 1
fi
grep -Fq "pid=$lighttpd_pid" <<<"$tcp_frontend"
grep -Eq '[[:space:]][^[:space:]]*:80[[:space:]]' <<<"$tcp_frontend"
grep -Eq '[[:space:]][^[:space:]]*:443[[:space:]]' <<<"$tcp_frontend"
udp_443=$(
  ss -H -lunp |
    awk '$4 ~ /:443$/ { print }' |
    sort
)
[[ -z "$udp_443" ]]

mapfile -t stage_matches < <(
  find /tmp -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 \
    \( -name 'caddy-package-audit-node-a.*' \
    -o -name 'caddy-repo-audit-node-a.*' \
    -o -name 'caddy-repo-install-node-a.*' \
    -o -name 'caddy-metadata-refresh-node-a.*' \
    -o -name 'caddy-inhibited-install-node-a.*' \) -print |
    sort
)
if ((${#stage_matches[@]} != 0)); then
  printf 'Unexpected Caddy staging path: %s\n' "${stage_matches[@]}" >&2
  exit 1
fi

mapfile -t apt_cache_files < <(
  find /var/cache/apt/archives -mindepth 1 -maxdepth 1 -type f \
    -name 'caddy_*.deb' -print |
    sort
)
printf 'caddy_apt_cache_file_count=%s\n' "${#apt_cache_files[@]}"
if ((${#apt_cache_files[@]} > 0)); then
  stat -c 'apt_cache=%F %U:%G %a %s %y %n' -- "${apt_cache_files[@]}"
  sha256sum -- "${apt_cache_files[@]}"
fi

printf 'identity_backup_residue_count=%s\n' \
  "$identity_backup_residue_count"
[[ "$identity_backup_residue_count" -eq 0 ]]
printf 'caddy_rollback_inspection_complete=true\n'
NODE_A_CADDY_ROLLBACK_INSPECTION
```

Expected effect:

- Independently revalidate the protected baseline, repository files, official
  candidate, architecture, and package-manager health.
- Require Caddy to be absent from dpkg installed/manual state, active identity
  databases, supplementary groups, package info, installed paths, systemd
  helper state, unit state, processes, masks, and start policy.
- Inspect account backup files by filename and boolean result only; never print
  password, shadow, or group contents.
- Require protected configuration hashes and services, lighttpd-only TCP
  80/443 ownership, unused UDP 443, and all action staging cleanup.
- Report any Caddy APT archive cache object as observational cache evidence
  without changing or automatically rejecting it.
- Perform no cleanup or other mutation.

Immediate validation:

- Require SSH exit `0`.
- Require zero active package, identity, path, systemd, process, policy, mask,
  and staging residue.
- Require zero Caddy references in inactive account backup files for strict
  rollback acceptance.
- Require protected hashes/services/listeners and
  `caddy_rollback_inspection_complete=true`.

Rollback boundary:

- None. Every command is read-only.
- Any discovered residue stops acceptance and requires a separately defined
  correction or an explicit decision to accept a non-active artifact.

  behavior directly, and record package-time start requests without relying on
  helper-specific human-readable APT messages.
- Mask `uuidd.service` and `uuidd.socket` before package configuration. The
  package may temporarily remove those masks through its generated `postinst`,
  but the exit-101 policy remains the activation barrier throughout the
  package transaction.
- After installation, disable the native units, disable SysV startup, stop both
  units, and reassert persistent masks. Remove the temporary start policy.
- Validate the exact package version/architecture/integrity; pinned SysV,
  service, and socket hashes; util-linux `2.38.1` command versions; locked
  non-root uuidd identity with `/run/uuidd` home and uuidd primary group; and
  `/var/lib/libuuid` as `uuidd:uuidd` mode `2775`.
- Require uuidd inactive/masked with no process and no SysV start links.
  Existing Caddy and lsyncd masks, protected services, listeners, protected
  configuration hashes, non-target package inventory, and dpkg integrity must
  remain unchanged. Existing autoremove candidates are never selected.

Expected effect:

- Only uuid-runtime is installed.
- At least one actual uuidd start request is recorded as inhibited after the
  direct exit-101 probe succeeds.
- `uuidd.service` and `uuidd.socket` finish inactive and persistently masked;
  no uuidd process or SysV start link remains.

  uuid_runtime_inhibited_install_complete=true
  ```

- Require the predeployment baseline

  `uuid_runtime_inhibited_install_complete=true`.

Bounded automatic rollback:

- After mutation starts, any failure stops uuidd, reasserts both masks, removes

### Action 16ar root cause and defined corrected retry

The accepted recovery evidence and a new Caddy `2.11.4` reload-lifecycle
regression establish the Action 16ar failure mechanism:

1. The journal proves the candidate configuration was accepted and loaded.
2. The historical driver entered only its post-reload readiness gate after
   that load.
3. Its `listener_snapshot` compared complete `ss -H -lntup` lines, including
   volatile PID/file-descriptor and queue details, byte-for-byte.
4. The container regression performed the exact logical
   bootstrap→candidate→bootstrap lifecycle. Unknown-host status changed
   `200→421→200`, the Caddy PID remained stable, and the semantic listener
   identity remained equal across both reloads. Both raw listener snapshots
   were unequal.
5. Therefore, healthy candidate and rollback reloads were misclassified as
   failures by the raw listener equality policy. This explains both the
   original readiness timeout and the false incomplete-rollback marker while
   remaining consistent with every accepted Action 16ar-a observation.

### Defined receiver-side validation/finalization protocol v2 (Action 17p-b)

The user authorized repository-only definition and validation of the
receiver-side protocol correction. No HA node was contacted, and no live
helper, SSH authorization, synchronization configuration, release, marker,
reconciliation unit, service, or Caddy selection was changed.

The definition is append-only. It does not modify the hash-pinned Action 17p
or Action 17p-a artifacts. Protocol v2 consists of:

- `manifests/synchronization-protocol-v2.yaml`, which records the intended
  transport, publication, finalization, reconciliation, and deployment gates.
- `templates/authorized-key-receiver-finalized-v2.in`, which binds the peer
  public key and source addresses to the v2 receiver with exactly the
  configured peer role; the key cannot select another incoming role.
- `scripts/publish-release-v2.sh`, which builds a release under a private
  staging name, validates it, writes the payload manifest, adds an empty
  `.finalize-request`, locks the tree, and makes it visible through one atomic
  rename. It never creates a sender `.complete`.
- `scripts/caddy-sync-release-receiver-v2`, which is designed for an
  authorized-key forced command pinned to exactly one peer source role. It
  accepts only the rsync server protocol, rejects deletion, scopes `rrsync` to
  that source role, and invokes finalization only after successful rsync
  completion.
- `scripts/finalize-incoming-release-v2.sh`, which runs as `caddy-sync`,
  applies one unique failure label to every fail-closed validation boundary,
  rejects unsafe manifest paths, extra or missing payload, symbolic links,
  hard links, special files, nested control files, invalid hashes,
  certificate/key mismatch, and invalid receiver-rendered Caddy
  configuration. It then creates `.complete.pending`, atomically renames it
  to `.complete`, and locks every directory/file to `0550`/`0440`.
- `templates/lsyncd-caddy-receiver-finalized-v2.lua.in`, which preserves the
  validated IPv6 source binding, never requests deletion, never transports
  `.complete` or `.complete.pending`, and does not preserve sender
  ownership/group/modes.
- `scripts/reconcile-release-v2.sh`, which considers only nonhidden releases
  containing a valid empty `.finalize-request` and receiver-generated
  `.complete`, rejects a pending marker and any payload/manifest mismatch,
  retains parent-revision conflict quarantine, and reloads Caddy only after
  complete validation.

The transported `.finalize-request` is a trigger, not evidence of completion.
It remains in the immutable tree so lsyncd does not continually retransmit a
receiver-deleted control file. Only the locally created `.complete` asserts
receiver validation.

Validation exercises the actual production publisher, finalizer, and
reconciler in Debian 12. The finalizer runs as `caddy-sync`; a valid fixture
prevents false negatives; the same function is run twice to prove idempotency;
and an unmanifested file prevents false positives. The reconciler activates a
validated release through a disposable container-local `systemctl` shim.
Arbitrary forced commands, remote deletion, unsafe manifest paths, historical
completion-marker transport, and readonly/local variable collisions are
rejected. The receiver-finalized lsyncd template parses under the installed
Debian lsyncd runtime.

### Defined read-only Node A `ssh -G` stderr diagnostic Action 17r-b

Action 17r-b is defined but has not been executed. The future exact command is:

```bash
cd /home/aaron/code/homelab-server-configs
Caddy/scripts/run-node-a-ssh-g-stderr-diagnostic-action17r-b.sh
```

OpenSSH documents `ssh -G` as evaluating `Host` and `Match` configuration,
printing the resulting effective client configuration, and exiting. The
OpenSSH portable implementation exits through its configuration-dump path
before connection or authentication. Action 17r-b therefore uses `ssh -G`
only to inspect effective IPv4 and IPv6 address-family, source-bind, hostname,
and host-key-alias values. It is not represented as a reachability or
restricted-transport probe, and both remote and workstation contracts require
`peer_connection_executed=false`.

One administrative SSH session enters `/` on Node A and streams the new
inspector through `sudo -n`. The administrative connection retains the
accepted workstation SSH-agent/configuration model and does not specify
`IdentitiesOnly=yes`. On Node A, the inspector runs the same non-connecting
IPv4 and IPv6 `ssh -G` commands used by Action 17r. It independently records
each command status and each parsed option.

Each stderr stream has separate assertions for byte bound, line bound, NUL
absence, printable content, secret-pattern exclusion, and supported
classification. The maximum is 1,024 bytes and four lines per address family.
Supported classifications are `empty`, `pseudo_terminal_not_allocated`,
`safe_unclassified`, and `unsafe_withheld`. Safe streams are represented by
byte count, line count, SHA-256, classification, and base64. Unsafe streams
are never encoded or emitted and use the literal `withheld` marker.

The workstation runner does not trust the remote safety decision. It decodes
each safe value into a protected temporary file and independently verifies the
byte count, line count, SHA-256, NUL absence, printable-content policy,
secret-pattern exclusion, and classification. It emits the remote transcript
only after both decoded streams and the transcript pass these gates. Every
observable condition has its own stable assertion label.

Before and after snapshots cover the retained release, synchronization key and
known-host state, Caddy selection, and relevant service state. The hashes must
match. The action cannot invoke a peer connection, restricted command, rsync,
helper, transfer, finalizer, marker mutation, reconciliation, service mutation,
or persistent mutation. Temporary paths are trap-managed; no live rollback is
required.

- Production-path regression:
  `061dc3007d298074679f948c74a9f46e1ac954bba1a1d44e6fb5bed34eb8f4c2`.

### Defined separately gated Caddy VRRP activation Action 20d

Action 20d is defined and validated on the workstation only. It is a
dual-node transaction with an explicit Node A-first activation order:

1. Node A must match its accepted main configuration, inactive fragment,
   helpers, services, DNS-VIP ownership, and absent Caddy-VIP baseline.
2. A protected copy of Node A's exact main configuration is retained, the
   single exact include
   `include /etc/keepalived/conf.d/caddy-ha.conf` is added atomically, and
   Keepalived is reloaded rather than restarted.
3. Bounded readiness requires Node A to report `CADDY_DUALSTACK=MASTER`, own
   exactly `10.1.0.56/22` and `fd36:5aa8:6971:1::56/128`, retain both DNS
   VIPs, pass the Caddy health helper, and preserve the Keepalived PID and
   restart count.
4. The same protected include/reload transaction runs on Node B, which must
   report `CADDY_DUALSTACK=BACKUP`, own neither Caddy VIP nor DNS VIP, pass
   health, and preserve its Keepalived PID and restart count.
5. Fresh read-only 20-assertion inspections on both nodes reconfirm a single
   dual-stack Caddy owner on Node A, Node B in `BACKUP`, unchanged DNS-VIP
   ownership, active services, exact fragments/helpers, and no post-check
   mutation.

Each node activation exports exactly 50 unique assertion labels. Each final
inspection exports exactly 26 unique assertion labels. The runner consumes
the producer inventories directly and rejects missing, duplicate, false,
contradictory, or unexpected evidence. It captures, hashes, classifies, and
emits bounded safe stdout and stderr during the original command. Unsafe
evidence is retained at a protected path rather than printed or deleted.

If Node A's remote transaction fails after its write, its local exit handler
restores the exact backup and reloads Keepalived. If Node B activation or any
final cross-node gate fails after Node A was accepted, the orchestrator rolls
back Node B first when necessary and Node A second. Each rollback restores
the exact pre-activation main configuration and requires the local Caddy VIPs
to be absent. An incomplete rollback exits `125` and emits
`manual_intervention_required=true`.

The installed and accepted fragment contains the Keepalived sync-group
`notify` directive. Therefore a future activation will invoke
`/usr/local/libexec/lsyncd-ha-failover-notify.sh` for the state transitions,
and that helper will make bounded asynchronous attempts to the locked Apprise
endpoint. This effect is included explicitly in the future activation
authorization boundary. Notification delivery is not an activation-success
gate because the helper is asynchronous and fail-open by design. Action 29
still owns independent notification delivery and monitoring acceptance.

not prove that WAN NAT/port forwarding is absent.

## Deferred Until After Core Deployment

- Home Assistant Yellow permanent ULA allocation and HAOS configuration,
  duplicate-address and reachability validation, reboot-persistence testing,
  and its authoritative AAAA and IPv6 PTR records are deferred until after
  core Caddy deployment acceptance. The current private operator source adds
  only `homeassistant.local.theama.co` A `10.1.2.120` with the corresponding
  canonical IPv4 PTR; neither record is deployed truth until a separately
  authorized activation and validation action succeeds.
- Live Munin monitoring installation, node/master configuration, and metric
  validation are deferred until after core Caddy deployment acceptance.
  Repository lint and fixture checks may run before deployment but do not
  authorize or represent live Munin deployment.
- Review the accumulated historical deployment test suite for streamlining
  after deployment acceptance. Identify redundant wrappers, fixtures, and
  repeated host/container coverage, but preserve immutable executed artifacts,
  authorization-hash provenance, false-positive and false-negative controls,
  security boundaries, and evidence needed to reconstruct accepted actions.
  Do not remove or consolidate historical tests during the active deployment.
- Build a manifest-driven focused validation runner after deployment
  acceptance. It must map each action to its exact host tests, Debian 12
  production slice, and shared policies so routine validation is reproducible
  without replaying unrelated immutable history.
- Replace best-effort detached Apprise delivery with a durable notification
  mechanism after deployment acceptance. Preserve non-blocking VRRP behavior,
  but add bounded retries or a persistent systemd-backed delivery queue,
  durable per-attempt journald evidence, duplicate suppression, and acceptance
  coverage for successful delivery, timeout, retry exhaustion, and recovery.
  The `2026-08-10` Node B BACKUP callback was invoked correctly but its current
  single curl attempt timed out after 5001 ms with exit 28, demonstrating the
  observability gap. Do not couple VRRP state transitions to notification
  delivery success.
- Production inventory and repository README updates.
- Canonical LikeC4 model and generated views.
- Invalid-release quarantine, interrupted-rsync recovery, revision-conflict,
  peer-reconnection, and rolling-upgrade drills. These are post-deployment
  reliability exercises, not core acceptance blockers.

## Post-Deployment Documentation Inputs

During deployment, record package versions, file paths, ownership, permissions,
configuration hashes, listener state, certificate details, DNS answers, VRRP
timings, synchronization results, monitoring output, notification delivery,
rollback locations, and every approved deviation. These observations become
the source for the post-deployment documentation set.

## Summary

Deploy Caddy on Nodes A and B as an independent dual-stack HA service:

- Caddy VIPs: `10.1.0.56/22` and `fd36:5aa8:6971:1::56/128`.
- Shared endpoint: `proxy.local.theama.co`.
- Initial application: `pihole-admin.local.theama.co`.
- Apprise endpoint: `http://10.1.3.83:8000/notify/apprise`.
- Preserve the existing Pi-hole DNS VIPs `.55` and `::55`.
- Move lighttpd to `127.0.0.1:8080`; Caddy owns VIP ports 80/443 and proxies the local Pi-hole UI.
- Use reciprocal lsyncd transport with Node A as the normal writer and guarded
  emergency publishing from Node B only with `--emergency` while Node B owns
  the coupled `PIHOLE_IPV4` and `PIHOLE_IPV6` MASTER state.
- Place the implementation under `homelab-server-configs/Caddy`; update DNS, monitoring, inventory, and canonical LikeC4 repositories for their respective concerns.
- Create operator documentation only after deployment and acceptance testing.

## Implementation Changes

### Packages, identities, and network preparation

Install or confirm on Nodes A and B:

- Caddy: `caddy`, `debian-keyring`, `debian-archive-keyring`, `apt-transport-https`, `ca-certificates`, `curl`, `gnupg`.
- HA and synchronization: `keepalived`, `lsyncd`, `rsync`, `openssh-client`, `openssh-server`.
- Validation and scripting: `openssl`, `jq`, `uuid-runtime`, `coreutils`, `findutils`, `util-linux`, `procps`, `iproute2`, `bash`.
- Monitoring: `munin-node`.
- Existing Pi-hole UI dependencies: `lighttpd` and its PHP/FastCGI packages.

Use the [official Caddy Debian package and systemd service](https://caddyserver.com/docs/install).
All Caddy, Keepalived, lsyncd, and custom-script output uses systemd-journald.
Validate journald retention during deployment; do not create duplicate file
logs or Caddy-specific logrotate rules.

Create:

- A restricted `caddy-sync` system account.
- A TLS-readable group containing only `caddy` and `caddy-sync`.
- Pinned SSH host keys and separate synchronization keys for each direction.
- Forced-command `authorized_keys` entries restricted by peer address, with shells, forwarding, PTYs, and agent forwarding disabled.

Install `/etc/sysctl.d/70-caddy-ha.conf`:

```text
net.ipv4.ip_nonlocal_bind = 1
net.ipv6.ip_nonlocal_bind = 1
```

Apply with `sysctl --system`. This allows both Caddy processes to bind the floating VIPs while Keepalived controls address ownership.

Permit through the internal firewall:

- Clients to Caddy VIPs on TCP 80/443.
- Clients to Caddy VIPs on UDP 443 for HTTP/3.
- VRRP protocol 112 only between Nodes A and B.
- Restricted synchronization SSH between Nodes A and B.
- Nodes A/B to `10.1.3.83:8000`.
- Munin master `10.1.3.83` to munin-node TCP 4949.
- Required outbound update and certificate-status traffic.

Create no external-zone ingress, public NAT, or WAN exposure.

### 2. Certificates and Caddy configuration

Add `prepare-certificate.sh` to consume the SSLs.com `.cert`, `.ca-bundle`, and `.key` files and generate:

- `leaf.pem`
- `intermediates.pem`
- `fullchain.pem`
- `privkey.pem`
- A non-secret manifest containing certificate fingerprint, SANs, issuer, expiry, public-key fingerprint, and content hashes

The script will:

- Confirm PEM formatting.
- Verify the `*.local.theama.co` SAN.
- Verify that the private key matches the leaf certificate.
- Reject encrypted, invalid, expired, or near-expiry material.
- Split the CA bundle and exclude a self-signed root from the chain served by Caddy.
- Verify the complete chain before publication.
- Set directories to `0750`, certificates to `0644`, and the private key to `0640 root:<TLS-group>`.
- Never commit certificates, private keys, webhook configuration, or SSH keys.

Configure Caddy with `tls <fullchain.pem> <privkey.pem>` as supported by the [Caddy TLS directive](https://caddyserver.com/docs/caddyfile/directives/tls). The complete intermediate chain will provide compatibility for modern iOS and Android devices without installing a private root certificate.

Create:

- `Caddyfile`: global settings, metrics, logging, timeouts, and imports.
- `conf.d/00-health.caddy`: `https://localhost`, returning a stable success response to `HEAD /`.
- `conf.d/10-pihole-admin.caddy`: `pihole-admin.local.theama.co` to `127.0.0.1:8080`.
- `conf.d/90-default-deny.caddy`: reject unknown hosts.
- `templates/reverse-proxy.caddy.example`: future application template.

Bind Caddy to the Caddy VIPs and loopback addresses. Keep its administration API and metrics on loopback. Enable per-host metrics at `127.0.0.1:2019/metrics` using [Caddy’s metrics support](https://caddyserver.com/docs/metrics).

Reconfigure lighttpd to:

- Listen only on `127.0.0.1:8080`.
- Disable its HTTPS listener.
- Preserve the existing Pi-hole PHP/FastCGI configuration.
- Deny network access to port 8080.
- Route error and access output through lighttpd's native syslog directives
  for systemd-journald capture.

The wildcard certificate covers `proxy.local.theama.co` and `pihole-admin.local.theama.co`, but not the `local.theama.co` apex or deeper multi-label names.

### Keepalived

The existing Pi-hole VRRPv3 instances are the single ownership authority:

| Setting | IPv4 | IPv6 |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Instance | `PIHOLE_IPV4` | `PIHOLE_IPV6` |
| DNS VIP | `10.1.0.55/22` | `fd36:5aa8:6971:1::55/128` |
| Caddy VIP | `10.1.0.56/22` | `fd36:5aa8:6971:1::56/128` |
| Node A priority | `150` | `150` |
| Node B priority | `100` | `100` |

Both instances remain members of `PIHOLE_DUALSTACK`; consequently all four
VIPs move together and the shared Caddy endpoint always reaches the current
DNS owner. The existing `check-dns` script remains the only tracked health
dependency. Caddy service state and endpoint health must never be added to the
DNS group, because a reverse-proxy failure is not authority to move DNS.

The separately deployed `CADDY_IPV4`, `CADDY_IPV6`, and `CADDY_DUALSTACK`
instances are retired through the separately gated Action 28l transition.
Their historical source and action artifacts remain preserved, but their live
fragment include must be absent after acceptance. Never allow the old and new
owners to advertise `.56/::56` concurrently.

Generate `/usr/local/libexec/check-caddy.sh` to require:

```bash
systemctl is-active --quiet caddy
caddy validate --config /etc/caddy/current/Caddyfile --adapter caddyfile
curl -k -I --fail --silent --show-error --max-time 3 https://localhost
```

The Caddy helper remains useful for monitoring and configuration acceptance,
but it no longer controls a VRRP instance. lsyncd, Munin, Apprise, and Caddy
failures raise alerts without moving DNS or Caddy VIP ownership.

### Bidirectional lsyncd and atomic reloads

Configure reciprocal streams:

- Node A outbound releases → Node B incoming/A.
- Node B outbound releases → Node A incoming/B.

Synchronize immutable, revisioned releases rather than live `/etc/caddy` files. Each release contains:

- Caddy configuration.
- Certificate files.
- Manifest and content hashes.
- Parent revision.
- Source node.
- Completion marker.

Disable remote deletion and exclude editor files, temporary files, runtime state, logs, and incomplete releases.

Node A is the normal writer. Node B publishing is allowed only when:

- Both coupled `PIHOLE_IPV4` and `PIHOLE_IPV6` instances report MASTER and
  Node B owns all four DNS/Caddy VIPs.
- Emergency mode is explicitly supplied.
- Its parent revision matches the active revision.

Quarantine divergent or concurrent revisions and notify the operator instead of resolving conflicts through timestamps.

Generate:

- `caddy-lsyncd.service`
- `caddy-sync-reconcile.path` and `.service`
- `caddy-sync-health.service` and `.timer`
- `caddy-cert-expiry.service` and `.timer`
- Caddy systemd override for release path, permissions, restart policy, and graceful reload
- lighttpd systemd override for loopback port 8080

The reconciler verifies release completeness, hashes, revision ancestry, certificate/key pairing, certificate chain, and Caddy configuration before atomically changing `/etc/caddy/current`.

The transactional reconciler performs `caddy validate` before promotion and
reload and restores the prior release on failure. The former independent
`caddy-validate-reload.path` and `.service` are retired because a second
path-triggered reload can race that transaction.

## Monitoring, Notifications, DNS, and Architecture

### Munin

Create these plugins in `homelab-monitoring-observability/Munin`:

- `caddy_health`: service status, health probe, VRRP state, VIP ownership.
- `caddy_requests`: request, error, status-code, and latency metrics.
- `caddy_tls`: certificate validity and remaining lifetime.
- `lsyncd_caddy`: service status, peer reachability, last successful reconciliation, revision lag, queued releases, failures, and quarantined conflicts.

Install configuration under `/etc/munin/plugin-conf.d/caddy-ha`, use unprivileged execution where possible, and validate with `munin-run`.

### Apprise notifications

Generate:

- `lsyncd-sync-failure-notify.sh`
- `lsyncd-ha-failover-notify.sh`

Both scripts will send JSON directly to:

```text
http://10.1.3.83:8000/notify/apprise
```

Payload contract:

```json
{
  "title": "Caddy HA notification",
  "body": "Event details",
  "type": "info|success|warning|failure",
  "format": "text"
}
```

The scripts will:

- Use short connection and total timeouts.
- Log delivery results to journald.
- Deduplicate repeated alerts.
- Execute asynchronously for Keepalived transitions.
- Never block VRRP state changes.
- Include hostname, VRRP state, VIP ownership, Caddy health, lsyncd state, active revision, peer lag, and failure details.

`lsyncd-sync-failure-notify.sh` will be called by systemd `OnFailure` and by the health timer after a configurable consecutive-failure threshold.

`lsyncd-ha-failover-notify.sh` will be invoked once by the `CADDY_DUALSTACK` sync group for MASTER, BACKUP, and FAULT transitions.

### DNS and inventory

Add to the Unbound local zone:

- `proxy.local.theama.co` A → `10.1.0.56`
- `proxy.local.theama.co` AAAA → `fd36:5aa8:6971:1::56`
- `pihole-admin.local.theama.co` A/AAAA → the Caddy VIPs
- IPv4 and IPv6 PTR for the VIPs → `proxy.local.theama.co`
- `_https._tcp.proxy.local.theama.co` SRV → priority 0, weight 0, port 443, target `proxy.local.theama.co`

Preserve `pihole.local.theama.co` on `.55` and `::55`.

Update inventory so Nodes A and B include `reverse_proxy`, `caddy`, and `lsyncd` responsibilities without storing secrets. Add OS name and version. FQDN's for hosted services.

### Architecture

Extend the canonical LikeC4 model with:

- Reverse-proxy platform.
- Caddy nodes and synchronization agents.
- Dual-stack Caddy VIP.
- External certificate artifact.
- Pi-hole admin proxy relationship.
- Munin monitoring and Apprise notification relationships.
- Named Caddy and lsyncd deployment instances on Nodes A and B.
- Caddy VIP deployment node.
- `reverse-proxy-ha` view.
- `reverse-proxy-failover` dynamic sequence.

Validate with `likec4 validate --json --no-layout`, repeating `--file` for every edited LikeC4 source.

## Test and Deployment Plan

Actions through accepted Action 28t completed conflict checks, inventory and
backups, package and service installation, Unbound record deployment, trusted
TLS and HTTP protocol validation, normal A-to-B protocol-v2 transfer, rejection
of ordinary Node B publishing, and coupled DNS/Caddy ownership. Do not replay
those completed phases or insert a separate post-Action 28t acceptance action.

The remaining core deployment has exactly two gates:

1. **Integrated coupled failover/failback and synchronization go-live
   transaction.** Actions 28u through 28aa are consumed and must not be
   rerun. Actions 28ab and 28ac are also consumed and must not be rerun. The
   Actions 28ad through 28ag are consumed and must not be rerun. Action 28ag
   proved failover, continuity, ordinary Node B publication rejection, and
   guarded emergency publication, then failed because it treated asynchronous
   receiver reconciliation and post-start VRRP convergence as immediate state.
   Its rollback restored the pre-Action 28af synchronization baseline. Action
   28ah is accepted and consumed. Exact authorized outer SHA-256
   `3143246804e33a9d2ed74c048279d1dcee21dc6b833707a0b92ab38df2b29838`
   returned `0`. It reinstated and activated synchronization, accepted only
   the exact known payload during startup replay, proved bounded emergency
   B-to-A and normal A-to-B reconciliation, completed controlled failover and
   failback with continuous DNS and HTTPS samples, and committed on both
   nodes. Node A is stable IPv4/IPv6 MASTER with all four shared VIPs; Node B
   is stable IPv4/IPv6 BACKUP with zero shared VIPs. Recovery was not invoked
   and manual intervention is not required. Action 28ah must not be rerun.
   It retains foreground `-nodaemon` journald logging and corrects the forced
   transport, deterministic finalization trigger, transactional reconciliation
   and reload rollback, and failed-only unit-reset boundaries. Its finalizer is
   derived from accepted stderr-safe finalizer SHA-256
   `15d858774a17369f31261f7f94bea72d575f269fdb3e8e991534f66dd4f4902d`,
   not the obsolete base finalizer rejected by Action 28ab. Action 28ah must
   retain the following transaction requirements:

   - consume accepted Action 28t and revalidate its required preconditions in
     the same run;
   - activate and validate lsyncd and reconciliation for go-live without making
     either a VRRP health dependency;
   - trigger a controlled Node A DNS/Keepalived ownership relinquish, not a
     Caddy-health-triggered DNS failover;
   - require bounded stable Node B IPv4/IPv6 MASTER state with all four
     DNS/Caddy VIPs, Node A with zero shared VIPs, continuous DNS and trusted
     HTTPS, and the shared Pi-hole interface identifying Node B;
   - prove ordinary Node B publication remains rejected and permit B-to-A
     replication only through the guarded `--emergency` publisher while Node B
     holds the accepted coupled MASTER state;
   - restore preferred Node A ownership and require bounded stable Node A
     IPv4/IPv6 MASTER state with all four VIPs, Node B BACKUP with zero shared
     VIPs, the shared interface identifying Node A, and healthy DNS, TLS,
     lsyncd, reconciliation, and release state;
   - retain stdout, stderr, statuses, transition timing, journals, notifier
     evidence, and rollback evidence under `/tmp`; notification delivery failure
     remains non-blocking; and
   - automatically recover or roll back when convergence fails, returning a
     distinct manual-intervention status if recovery cannot be proven.

   Historical Action 18c-vrrp-a and Action 18c must not execute: their separate
   `CADDY_DUALSTACK` assumptions are obsolete. The new transaction must use the
   active coupled `PIHOLE_IPV4`/`PIHOLE_IPV6` ownership contract.

2. **Final read-only deployment acceptance snapshot — complete.** Action 29k
   returned `0` and verified stable dual-node DNS/Caddy ownership; A, AAAA,
   PTR, and SRV answers through both resolvers; trusted certificate identity
   and HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and HTTP/3; shared and node-specific Pi-hole
   interfaces; current release and bidirectional protocol-v2 state; active
   lsyncd/reconciliation; absence of transaction residue; and the actual
   versions, hashes, paths, permissions, timings, and approved deviations.
   Core deployment is accepted. The complete historical host/Podman suite was
   not run.

The post-acceptance mobile sign-off is complete: Android Chrome was manually
tested successfully, and the operator waived a separate iOS Safari test and
accepted it as passed. Munin deployment, Home Assistant Yellow ULA work,
documentation, and the deferred reliability exercises remain under their
separate post-deployment scopes.

Acceptance requires:

- Exactly one owner for both Caddy VIPs.
- Successful trusted TLS from the automated workstation acceptance; Android
  Chrome passed manual testing and iOS Safari passed by explicit operator
  waiver.
- Continued Pi-hole admin access after failover.
- Active and validated lsyncd/reconciliation, normal A-to-B synchronization,
  rejection of ordinary Node B publishing, and guarded B-to-A replication only
  with `--emergency` while Node B is coupled MASTER.
- Proven Apprise callback invocation and at least one successful delivery;
  individual best-effort delivery failure is non-blocking.
- Accepted Action 22 Default-LAN-only firewall disposition with no trigger that
  requires reevaluation.
- No regression to the existing DNS VIP cluster.

Munin metrics are acceptance criteria for the separately authorized
post-deployment monitoring phase, not for core Caddy deployment acceptance.

## Post-Deployment Documentation and Reliability

Only after acceptance, create:

- `Caddy/README.md`
- `Caddy/docs/QUICK_START.md`
- `Caddy/docs/INSTALLATION.md`
- `Caddy/docs/UNINSTALLATION.md`
- `Caddy/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md`
- Mermaid architecture and failover diagram
- LikeC4 source/view documentation and generated-view provenance

Reliability defaults:

- Retain the last ten validated releases per node.
- Alert at 30, 14, and 7 days before certificate expiry.
- Renew certificates through staged releases; never overwrite live files.
- Upgrade Node B first, fail over intentionally, then upgrade Node A.
- Run quarterly IPv4/IPv6 failover and mobile TLS tests.
- Keep lsyncd outside the VRRP health dependency.
- Keep Caddy administration and metrics loopback-only.
- Preserve `PIHOLE_DUALSTACK` as the ownership authority and keep reverse-proxy
  health out of its tracked dependencies so reverse-proxy problems cannot
  remove or move DNS service.
- Treat automated DNS-challenge renewal as a future enhancement.
